evidence.citation: Rufinus Historia ecclesiastica10.9, full Latin Frumentius/Edesius chapter
evidence.finding: The full newly read chapter directly follows Frumentius from Meropius’s young relative to the unnamed king’s records official, assistant to the regent/child king and promoter of Roman merchants’ Christian meetings, then his report to Athanasius and episcopal commission back to India. Rufinus expressly identifies former companion Edesius, later a presbyter in Tyre, as his personal informant. This adds a concrete early literary witness and its claimed chain of testimony to the already-closed Frumentius source core.
evidence.qualification: This is an already-closed identity receiving a new original source, not a new whole-identity closure. The king is unnamed, Athanasius is only recently installed, and the chapter gives no exact birth/death or modern conversion year. Ousanas/Ezana identification and literal modern Ethiopia-vs-India geography are not silently read into the Latin. Rufinus’s reported apostolic miracles are source testimony, not independently proved events; the return/commission is an activity sequence, not a first-career date.
evidence.accounting: One genuinely new named primary target; already-read owned source passages are retained as old evidence, not counted again.

evidence.excerpt:
季布也。”猛大笑。
  秦王坚自鄴如枋头,宴父老,改枋头为永昌,复之终世。甲寅,至长安,封慕容为新兴侯;以燕故臣慕容评为给事中,皇甫真为奉车都尉,李洪为驸马都尉,皆奉朝请。李邽为尚书,封衡为尚书郎,慕容德为张掖太守,燕国平睿为宣威将军,悉罗腾为三署郎。其馀封授各有差。衡,裕之子也。
  燕故太史黄泓叹曰:“燕必中兴,其在吴王乎!恨吾老,不及见耳!”汲郡赵秋曰:“天道在燕,而秦灭之。不及十五年,秦必复为燕有。”
  慕容桓之子凤,年十一,阴有复仇之志。鲜卑、丁零有气干者,皆倾身与之交结。权翼见而谓之曰:“儿方以才望自显,勿效尔父不识天命!”凤厉色曰:“先王欲建忠而不遂,此乃人臣之节;君侯之言,岂奖劝将来之义乎!”翼改容谢之,言于秦王坚曰:“慕容凤忼慨有才器,但狼子野心,恐终不为人用耳。”
  秦省雍州。
  是岁,仇池公杨世卒,子纂立,始与秦绝。叔父武都太守统与之争国,起兵相攻。

evidence.citation: Thorigny CIL XIII3162, all THREE complete inscribed units including both copied letters; RIB1280 full edition/diplomatic text, apparatus and internal-date context
evidence.finding: Thorigny’s main face directly names TIBERIUS CLAUDIUS PAULINUS as legate of LUGDUNENSIS, then explicitly says the SAME man later served as legate in BRITAIN with the sixth legion, with Sollemnis attending him. The copied Paulinus letter itself addresses Sennius Sollemnis and discusses gifts, a future military commission and pay; the Aedinius letter explicitly makes Paulinus his predecessor. This is a concrete original inter-office identity bridge. RIB1280 independently preserves TibClPau[...], the restored legate name/rank and a building carried out SUB CURA in the emperor Antoninus’s TRP III/COS III setting, internally dated to220 under Elagabalus. This supplies a real active early-third-century governing context, unlike a retrospective honor’s bare catalogue date. The separate owned law addresses a serving EpirusNova governor under Valentinian/Valens in372: keeping the two named provincial-source scopes as one ordinary adult career would require another152years after Paulinus’s220 command. Propose their clear chronological source separation.
evidence.qualification: The exact RIB reading is partly restored and its imperial name/numerals are erased; preserve the published apparatus and internal220 dating rather than claiming unbroken stone text. The Thorigny base’s Pius/Proculus subscription dates its238 installation; the copied letters are earlier and it does not prove Paulinus or Aedinius survived238, died238, or personally wrote then. A letter’s promised future commission is not an already held post for Sollemnis; the twenty-five-thousand sestertii is his pay, not Paulinus’s age. The220 SUB CURA commission and372 governor address are the positive chronological discriminator, not merely a152year gap between potentially posthumous monuments. Unknown biological endpoints remain null and game228 death is not applied to the Epirus person.
evidence.accounting: One new named target record; number of monuments, diploma copies or differently named people inside the composite is not inflated into extra completed roster people.

evidence.finding: The full Tarraco honor explicitly names QUINTUS HEDIUS, son of LUCIUS, POLLIA tribe, RUFUS LOLLIANUS GENTIANUS: augur, consul, proconsul of Asia, census/legation roles in Lugdunensis and Hispania citerior, curator of Puteoli and Velitrae, commander of XXII Primigenia and tribune of VII Gemina. The second honor explicitly names Quintus Hedius Lollianus Gentianus as Hispania citerior governor, with his own corn clerks, commentarienses and speculatores listed separately. This independently establishes the full Hedius core beyond the modern biography. The separate Moesian fragment III7516 prints Cosco/[nium Gentianum] in its Commodus imperial/legate context; ILB642 prints abbreviated COS GEN beside a partially restored Cn Suellius Rufus. Most decisively for the abbreviated Cosconius core, the newly viewed actual Ashmolean coin photograph has the legible reverse COSC GENTIANOU within the Nicopolis-ad-Istrum legend, opposite Septimius Severus. These are concrete different full-name/province source cores. No original object read here states that Cosconius is an alternative nomen of Hedius or joins the two careers.
evidence.qualification: The coin object catalogue assigns196 according to RPC; there is no engraved CE year, so196 is an editorial dating, not an exact life endpoint. CILIII7516 is heavily restored, including much of the provincial title and imperial titulature; its190–193 catalogue interval is not a birth/death date. ILB642 has damaged abbreviations and a catalogue198 date: it must not by itself create a certain simultaneous two-governor career. The Hedius honors have null numeric dates. VI1978 partly RESTORES the Hedius cognomina in a dated priest-admission series; admission is not birth and the surrounding other priests are not relatives. The separately read157–159 Lucius Hedius Rufus Lollianus AVITUS texts are not assigned to Quintus Gentianus. Different nomina and distinct provincial careers support conservative key separation, not biological proof that a polyonymous official could never bear both names; whole identity remains unclosed.
